column1: #The mod's own windows for OpenHOI3 (script/openhoi/windows). Read by OpenHOI3 alone: the original does not open this folder.

A trade decision can be unavailable even when a country has resources spare: each trade applies a two day cooldown that blocks the buy decision while it is handled. Wait and watch your decisions.

The focus can be changed at any time, but the effects are not instant: a new focus takes about 90 days before it gives anything, and the old one wears off over as long as it was active for. Bonuses come in three tiers, reached after 90, 360 and 720 days.
Progress towards the next building each of your ministers will place. The counters are maintained by the AI, so nothing on this page can be set.

Never configured - showing defaults. Apply to adopt them.

How far into the red per day the AI may sell a resource. While a stockpile is above "Sell above", the AI sells that resource's daily balance plus this amount, drawing the stockpile down by up to this much a day. It cancels its sales once the daily balance falls below minus this amount.

Daily surplus is how much of a resource the AI keeps coming in each day beyond what the country actually needs. It only sells once the stockpile is above "Sell above", and cancels its own purchases once the stockpile is above "Stockpile". Supplies are left to the AI's own judgement.
Another category already uses this priority

This only takes effect with "Prioritize Upgrades/Custom" selected in the production window. IC is handed out in priority order, starting at 1, and each priority may only be used once. A category that cannot be paid for in full takes whatever is left and the ones after it get nothing. Anything still unspent goes to production. Amount is read either as a share of what the category needs or as a flat IC figure, depending on its mode.

Upgrades and reinforcement can be capped so an emergency cannot swallow the whole budget. Supply can be given a stockpile goal, which it puts a little extra IC towards until it is reached. Consumer goods can take 50% more IC while there is dissent.
The engine will not take more than $N$
Keeps producing officers for 10 more days, for a buffer of around 500

This only takes effect with "Slider AI" selected in the technology window. The numbers are resource amounts rather than slider positions: once a resource falls below its lower threshold the AI produces it until the upper threshold is reached, and how much leadership that takes is its own decision.

Officers cannot be set above 110, which is an engine limit. Diplomacy takes influences already running into account. Leadership is handed out to officers first, then spies, then diplomacy, and research takes whatever is left.

Every battle is added as it finishes and kept with the savegame. Loading an earlier save brings back the record as it stood then. The Total column adds unlike things: a naval battle's losses are ships, a raid's are of another kind again.
Nothing recorded for $TAG$ yet. Battles are added as they finish.

No province has any of this.
Each shade starts at the amount under it. $COUNT$ provinces have any. The scale runs from the 1% with the least to the 1% with the most, so everything above $TOP$ shares the top shade.
Levels 1 to 10, the same ladder the infrastructure map climbs.
Grey: none here - light where you can see the province, dark where not.
Grey: nothing to show. Only provinces you have the intel for - your own and your allies' - show any supply. The rest are dark grey.
§GRight click§W for what else this map mode can show.

How many days the supplies in the province last its units, at what they use a day. Each shade starts at the number of days under it. The game keeps a province stocked for 35 days of its need, so a well supplied one sits in the top shade. Only provinces with units that use supplies are shaded.

How many days the fuel in the province lasts its units, at what they use a day. Each shade starts at the number of days under it. The game keeps a province stocked for 35 days of its need, so a well supplied one sits in the top shade. Only provinces with units that use fuel are shaded.

How far the province is from the depot that supplies it. Supply is handed along province by province, so the further it has to travel, the less of it arrives. Poor infrastructure makes a province count as two or three instead of one, so a route across bad ground is further than it looks on the map. Each shade starts at the number under it. Depots themselves are the top shade, provinces with no supply line at all the bottom one, and land in no supply network is grey.

How much of that distance is poor infrastructure rather than real distance. Zero means the way to the depot is good all the way and costs nothing extra. Eight means the route counts as eight provinces longer than it really is, because of what it crosses. This is the number that building infrastructure brings down. Provinces with no supply line at all show nothing.

How much of what the province can pass on in a day is asked of it today - its own units' shortfall and what provinces further out want through it. Each shade starts at the share under it. At 100% the line through here is full, and anything beyond waits. How much a province can pass on is the game's own figure, worked out from the province's modifiers and its controller's.
The same for fuel, which shares the province's capacity figure: how much of what it can pass on in a day is asked of it today. At 100% the line through here is full.

What a load of supplies or fuel loses crossing the province - the same amount whatever the size of the load, so a long line of small loads loses the most. Half on the controller's own ground, more in mud unless the ground is frozen, more again where partisans are active in occupied land, less with the controller's supply technologies. Each shade starts at the tax under it. Land in no supply network is grey.
Supplies passed on through the province today, on their way out from the depot - the supply lines themselves.
Fuel passed on through the province today, on its way out from the depot.
Supplies in the province. A capital's are the country's whole stockpile, so it sits in the top shade.
Fuel in the province. A capital's is the country's whole stockpile, so it sits in the top shade.
This game does not collect statistics: the rule was turned off in the lobby.
Writes every country's every statistic as a file, in the layout the plotting tool reads

§YGame statistics, kept in your savegame.§W
Every day the game notes each country's figures, so that you can plot them later on the utility's Statistics page:
 - leadership and how it is shared out
 - spies and neutrality
 - IC, its efficiency and the production sliders
 - the popularity of each ideology
 - provinces owned and controlled, units and manpower
 - stockpiles, daily balance and trade of each resource

§GNothing about you or your computer is collected, and nothing is sent anywhere.§W
The record is part of the savegame and adds about half a megabyte to it for each year played. Turn this off to keep saves smaller.
Draws every series into the same axes instead of one plot each

§YLets a player in whose OpenHOI3 checksum does not match the host's.§W
The checksum as calculated by the original game still has to match, but it does not cover all of the game files.

§RIf the mismatched files cause the players' simulations to differ, the game will be resynced each midnight.§W

§YRecords the game, so that it can be played back later.§W\nThe recording is kept beside your savegames, and every save remembers its place in the timeline. A game can be played back from its start up to the selected save. You can also create a new save during the replay and continue playing from there.\n - In multiplayer only the host records the game, and only the host can watch the replay.

§YPlays back the game that led to this save.§W
The game runs again from its start, through every save and load made on the way, up to this save. You only look on: nothing you press changes the game. Pause and speed work as usual.
 - Select a country on the map first to watch the game through its eyes. With none selected you watch the country that played.
It is made of $COUNT$ recordings, and the game is loaded once for each.

§RThis replay was recorded with another engine version or other rules.§W

 - this engine: $NOW$
You can watch it, but it may not play back as it was played. Where the game goes another way, the replay stops.
The replay no longer fits this engine and stops here
Replay: the game was saved and loaded here...
§YLook on through another country.§W\nShows that country's screens, its units and what it knows of the map. Countries marked with * were played by a person. The game being played back is not changed.

§YWrites this save and its replay as one file.§W
The file can be given to another player, who imports it with Import replay. It is written to:
$FOLDER$
It only plays back with the same engine version and the same game files.

$FOLDER$

A step is named as the engine names it. Click a heading to sort by it, and again to turn the order round. An indented line is a part of the step above it and is counted in that step as well. Parts that run side by side on several processor threads can add up to more than their step.
